messages.subject: Re: Non-continuous SEM: Goodnes of Fit indices
parts:
Hi,

> On 20 May 2019, at 10.01, Lilia Heinrich <lilia...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> Hi,
> R lavaan calculates -compared to Stata (gsem)- all imaginable Goodnes of Fit indices for non-continuous SEM.

Stata’s GSEM and Lavaan do quite different analysis when using categorical and other non-continuous outcomes. Lavaan follows the limited information approach used by Mplus where each indicator is assumed to have an underlying latent variable. Estimation starts by calculating the correlation matrix between the latent variables and the SEM model is then fitted to this estimated correlation matrix. The saturated model and null model that are required for model testing and most model fit statistics are about this estimated correlation matrix.

Stata’s GSEM on the other hand uses full information approach, without estimating a correlation matrix as an intermediate step. This requires numerical integration over the latent variables, which is very time consuming. Because no covariance matrices are fitted, model fit indices calculated based on covariance fit do not exist.

See e.g. this presentation for an explanation of the difference between these approaches

https://personality-project.org/r/tutorials/summerschool.14/rosseel_sem_cat.pdf

> Somebody told me recently that the use and assessment of GOF for non-continuous SEM isn`t recommended. Does anyone know more about this issue that here? Why is not recommended? Literature recommendation?

I would ask that somebody what is the justification for his/her opinion.

I do not see a reason not to report the fit indices produced by Mplus or Lavaan. In Stata, you do not get these indices, but I do not see a reason why you could not calculate them manually. For example, estimating a saturated model using the same links and distribution as your main model, and comparing these using likelihood ratio test would be analogous to a normal chi2 test and would seem a good idea to me. However, I am not aware of any literature that would explore this idea.

More generally, this is not really about Lavaan and you can probably get a more thorough answer and loads of reference from SEMNET email list. http://www2.gsu.edu/~mkteer/semnet.html

Mikko
